subject: Orchid Labs — concession request for delayed long-seq support
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Orchid Labs — customer asks for concession tied to long-seq support delay

Team,

Orchid Labs (Tara Singh) pinged this morning asking for a commercial concession. Short summary: they planned a production launch that depends on our long-sequence (long-seq) support and a quant rollout. The feature missed the internal target we communicated; their integration hit a hard blocker and they are asking for a one-time credit while they re-baseline their launch. Attached: orchid_request.pdf (customer note) and their expected 90-day usage/forecast.

Concrete asks from me:
- Advice on an approvable concession amount (ballpark $ or % of quarterly committed spend).
- Evidence/product messaging we can share with customer about mitigations and timing.
- Approval path: who needs to sign off for $X credits?

Context: deal ORCH-2028-Q3 — pilot is active, projected first-month spend $45k, ramp to $120k/mo by month 3. They specifically call out latency degradation > 2x for sequences > 8k tokens during our quant rollout. They want a provisional credit and a firm timeline.

I want to draft a joint reply that is commercially sympathetic but preserves margin. Recommended next step: quick sync (15m) or a set of proposed concessions we can put to Tara today.

Attaching: orchid_request.pdf and q2_latency_breakdown.csv.

—Marcus
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Labs — customer asks for concession tied to long-seq support delay

Thanks Marcus — quick product update to inform the commercial ask.

What happened: the quant rollout introduced a kernel scheduling fallback for sequences > 6k in the current optimizer path; that fallback restores correctness but increases per-token latency for certain GPU topologies. We originally estimated the impact would be transient and mitigated by a micro-optimization in late Aug; that optimization slipped into mid-Sept due to a validation regression.

Mitigations we can offer immediately:
- Turn on an internal fast-path for Orchid (canary) that pins a more aggressive kernel selection (works for their model family) — requires engineering enablement and a config flag (2–4 business days).
- Provide temporary larger token-budget allotment on their Dedicated pool to avoid fallback behavior (operational workaround).
- Beta access to prefix/KV prefetch cache (reduces end-to-end latency for long contexts) — product team can enable but we should attach an explicit testing window.

Recommended commercial posture:
- Small one-time credit to acknowledge impact: equivalent to 2 weeks of expected run-rate (their forecast => ~$60k) rather than larger makewhole.
- Combine credit with a timeline + technical mitigation offer (canary + prefetch trial).

I'm attaching a short roadmap excerpt and rough latency delta table (roadmap_excerpt.pdf). If you want, Karthik and I can draft a proposed customer note that pairs a modest credit with the concrete mitigations above.

—Laura
Sr. PM, Model Serving
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-22T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Labs — customer asks for concession tied to long-seq support delay

Appreciate the context. From finance/comm ops perspective:

- Approval bands: up to $25k can be approved by Sales Director (Marcus). $25k–$75k requires revenue leader signoff (VP Sales). Anything > $75k needs Exec (GM/CRO) approval and must be routed through RevOps for contract amendment.
- Impact math: if we grant 2 weeks at projected ramp that Laura noted (~$60k) that exceeds Marcus' direct approval. If mechanics are credits against future invoices (preferred) we can do a conditional clause: credit is applied if customer stays at >80% of forecast for next 2 months.
- Tax/recognition: credits >$50k will need accounting treatment and may affect quota calculations — flag to SalesOps.

My recommendation: ask for a reduced ask from the customer (1 week / ~$30k) and pair with technical mitigations and a conditional clause. If the customer insists on the full 2-week figure, route to execs with a short approval memo.

I can draft the finance memo this afternoon if you want to escalate.

—Priyom
Head of Commercial Operations
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-24T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Labs — customer asks for concession tied to long-seq support delay

Quick technical ask before we lock the commercial language:

- Marcus: can you share the customer-observed token distribution and specific examples where latency > 2x? The q2_latency_breakdown.csv is helpful, but we need sequence-level traces to validate the fast-path applicability.
- Laura: if we enable the canary fast-path, what is the expected rollback plan if we hit a correctness edge-case? I want the mitigation/rollback steps in writing we can attach to the customer note.

If we can commit to: (a) canary enablement in 48–96h, (b) rollback within 2 hours if anomalies observed, and (c) a follow-up validation window, then I'm comfortable recommending the smaller conditional credit.

Attaching: longseq_impact_notes.md (internal notes).

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@orchidlabs.com>
Cc: Orchid Labs Billing <billing@orchidlabs.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Labs — concession request and next steps

Tara — thanks for the patience while we reviewed this internally. I wanted to summarize what we can offer and the next steps so you have a single note from us. (Internal thread below for reference.)

What Redwood is offering now:
- Technical mitigation: we can enable a targeted canary fast-path for Orchid's model family within 2–4 business days. This is a configuration change, not a code push. We will include a 72-hour monitoring window and a defined rollback plan should anything unexpected surface.
- Commercial: a conditional one-time credit equivalent to one week of your projected run-rate (~$30k). The credit is conditional on Orchid maintaining >=80% of the forecasted usage for the two months following the canary enablement.
- Optional: trial access to prefix/KV prefetch cache (beta) for the duration of the pilot, which should materially reduce long-context latency.

If the above is acceptable, please reply with a brief confirmation and we will circulate a short amendment to the pilot terms (RevOps will prepare). If you prefer a larger unconditional concession we can escalate to leadership, but that will take additional time and formal approval.

Attachments: proposed_mop.pdf (operational playbook for canary + rollback).

Looking forward to your reply — happy to jump on a quick call with the team.

—Marcus
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
